frames.caption: Both experts are sure of every pixel, variance 0.01. Each pixel's product has mean 0 and sd 0.071, and that mean is 10 of each expert's standard deviations from its own mean.
Now the cat's training images share one head and vary in body; the dog's share one body and vary in head. So the cat is loose on the body, the dog on the head.
Precisions add and the mean is precision-weighted, pixel by pixel. A head pixel weighs the cat's 100 against the dog's 1: 99/101 = 0.980.
Keep the mosaic's body and make the dog sure on the head too, variance 0.01. log Z measures how much the two experts overlap.
A sure +1 against a sure −1 adds −98.96 to log Z per pixel; sure against loose adds −2.904. Drag the variances between mosaic and blend.
Each animal now sits in the left or the right half, ½ each, sure there and loose (mean 0) elsewhere. Multiplying two mixtures gives one component per pair: four.
A same-half pair puts sure +1 against sure −1 on 8 pixels: ℓ = −803.2. A side-by-side pair meets loose pixels, ℓ = −24.1, so side-by-side pairs hold all but e⁻⁷⁷⁹ of the weight.
The forward process noises each expert: a cat head pixel becomes variance 0.505, a dog head pixel 1.0. Adding their scores gives the score of these noised experts' product.
The cat's lead falls from 100 : 1 to 1.98 : 1, so summed scores aim the head at 0.233. The noised product, the correct target, puts it at 0.693.
Head +0.980, body −0.980: a cat head on a dog body. log Z −46.5.
